Latent 1/2 and the 8K training length rest on q0 only (8K on our 8K-length eval, which cannot see the long-document benefit of 32K). Load balancing is not negative entropy: its loss is only 0–0.007 below DSV3 (single-seed noise about ±0.008), level in the PROD setting (PROD1_PHI − PROD1_DPSK ≈ 0), and with negative entropy only (no expert bias) the router is unhealthy.

KD loss variants compared: same α 0.8, same MuonH

The 8 runs differ only in how the teacher distribution is truncated in the KD term: α = 0.8, MuonH optimizer, seed 1 and data order are identical; the baseline is still CE (MuonH, α = 0); B64 (top-64 + the rest of the tail as one bucket) is KD α 0.8 itself and is drawn as a line too, so each variant can be read against it. Negative = better than CE.

Naming: letters = tail treatment · number = top-k size · trailing Y = y computed exactly
PartMeaning
BBucket: the tail outside the top-k is merged into one outcome; only the student's total tail mass has to match
SSampled: the tail is estimated from the 4 tokens pre-sampled in the cache (unbiased)
DDData Draw: instead of the teacher's tail, the corpus's actual next token approximates it
DROPTail dropped: the teacher is renormalised over the top-k only (control)
64 / 128how many top-k tokens are computed exactly
Yy exact: when the actual next token y falls outside the top-k, y is taken out of the tail and computed exactly

Data derisk and 2.5 vs 2.6

Data: the 80B KD corpus pre-packed into 32K rows (pack plan e9r500: a row is several document blocks that do not attend to each other), teacher cache = tc_80b, seed 1 (the plan fixes the data order).
Experiment: the MUONH_FIT base trained on the same plan with CE / KD 2.6 / KD 2.5, to check the new data pipeline, the KD gain on the new data, and teacher 2.5 vs 2.6. All KD: α 0.8 (KD 0.8 + CE 0.2), tail S64Y.
Every checkpoint is evaluated twice: 8K window (long documents chunked at 8192, as in every earlier experiment, directly comparable) and 32K window (chunked at 32768, matching the training length).

Document mask: mask vs no mask (KD MiMo-2.6, α 0.8, S64Y; plus Boxiang's old-LR no-mask run; all minus the same CE (OPT_MUONH, old LR), more negative is better)

All three lines are KD MiMo-2.6 teacher, α 0.8, S64Y, the same KD data (650B), softmax router, no SWA. Mask = each document in a packed 8K sequence attends only to itself (Megatron --dataloader-inter-document-masking). Grey and purple are our pair, both at the fitted MuonH LR law, differing only in the mask: their distance = the effect of the mask. Blue is Boxiang's original run at the old LR (original ArchScale law), no mask: blue and grey differ only in the LR. Each point = seed mean − OPT_MUONH (where q0 has 3 seeds they are averaged into one point). Note: the eval is doc-isolated (every document scored alone), the same condition the masked run trains under.

Router choice

Zero line = MUONH_FIT: MuonH, fitted LR law (fit, q0 peak 0.0164), plain CE (no KD), 128-choose-8 MoE, full attention (no SWA / sink), the vanilla softmax router + Switch aux loss 1e-3, AdamH gate at LR ×1.

softmax router

  • Softmax over the logits of the 128 experts; the 8 highest scores are picked.
  • Load balance by an aux loss (Switch style, coefficient 1e-3): when some experts are picked too often, an extra penalty pushes the router to spread the tokens.
    • How it works: in every MoE layer and every micro-batch (32,768 tokens), two things are measured: fi = the fraction of tokens actually sent to expert i, Pi = the mean softmax probability these tokens give expert i. aux = 1e-3 × 128 × Σi fi·Pi, in effect added to the training loss and back-propagated with it. fi is only a count with no gradient; the gradient flows through Pi: the more tokens an expert gets (larger fi), the more its probability is pushed down.
  • The micro-batch size (set in the ladder's per-rung layout table, chosen for memory) decides how many tokens each aux statistic covers:
    rungnodesmicro-batchtokens per aux statisticEP
    q04432,7681
    q18432,7681
    q216432,7681
    q316432,7684
    q432216,3848
    q56418,1928
    q66418,1928
    • EP (expert parallelism): the 128 experts are stored across several GPUs, each holding 128 ÷ EP of them (q3: 4 GPUs with 32 each; q4-q6: 8 GPUs with 16 each). In every layer the router first picks the 8 experts for the tokens on its own GPU, then an all-to-all sends each token to the GPU holding its experts, which computes it and sends the result back. It only saves memory and does not change the result; the routing choice and the aux statistics are done on the GPU's own micro-batch before the tokens are sent, so it does not affect the aux loss either.

DSV3 router

  • Each expert score goes through its own sigmoid, each in 0-1, not competing with the others.
  • Experts are picked by “score + bias”. Every expert has a bias that is not a trained parameter but adjusted by a rule every step: an overloaded expert gets bias − 0.001, an underloaded one + 0.001.
  • The bias only decides which experts are picked, not their output weights: after the 8 are picked, their weights are their original sigmoid scores (without the bias), normalised over those 8 (Megatron moe_utils.py L953-959).
  • A small aux loss is kept as well (seq aux 1e-4), computed per sequence.
    • How it works: the same formula as the Switch aux above, but measured over each 8K training sequence (one packed row, possibly several documents), with a 10× smaller coefficient. Per sequence: fi = the fraction of its tokens sent to expert i, Pi = the mean score its tokens give expert i (each token's 128 sigmoid scores first normalised to sum to 1). aux = 1e-4 × 128 × Σi fi·Pi, computed for each of the 4 sequences of a micro-batch and averaged; again only Pi carries a gradient. Being per sequence, it does not depend on the micro-batch size.
  • Design idea: balance mainly by the bias and hardly by an aux loss, so the aux loss does not interfere with the main task.
Which optimizer and LR for the gate (router weights)

The gate is the weight matrix Wg (128 × width) that computes the logits.

  • AdamH: the MuonH default - Adam updates, but the weights are kept on a sphere of fixed radius (hyperball); the weight norm cannot grow.
  • AdamW: plain AdamW; the weight norm is free (wd 0 in B2).
  • router LR ×1: the gate uses the same LR as the body (0.0164 at q0 under the fitted law).
  • router LR ×0.19: the gate LR is lowered to ~3.1e-3, about the AdamW baseline own LR level. The earlier probe B1 showed that an AdamW gate at ×1 saturates the logits, hence 0.19.

Router health statistics

Health from the router monitor of Boxiang (DECISIONS 10-26 19:1x-19:2x): DSV3 at q1-q3 has expert bias 3-5 (pre-registered limit 1) and runaway logits 60-87, load balanced only by the bias - not adoptable as is under the pre-registered rule; DSV3 + AdamW gate + router LR ×0.19 pins ~10 % of the selected experts' scores near 1, bias above 1, logits rising; DSV3 + router LR ×0.19 is healthy. The two pathologies have different causes: at router LR ×1 the AdamH gate of DSV3 does not learn the balance itself and the bias keeps growing, which router LR ×0.19 fixes; the two ×0.19 arms share the router LR and only the one with the AdamW gate pins the selected scores near 1, so the pinning comes from the AdamW gate itself (DECISIONS 10-26 17:29).

Negative-entropy balance loss

Negative-entropy balance loss: every layer keeps an EMA (η 0.65) of the router probabilities, me = the long-run mean probability of expert e (measured over the whole global batch, updated once per step); loss = α·E·Σe pe·(log me + 1), pe = the mean probability the current tokens give expert e; the bracket carries no gradient, only pe does. Effect: experts used a lot over time (large me) are pushed down, rarely used ones pulled up, driving the mean routing toward uniform (maximum entropy). It replaces the original balance loss (seq aux 1e-4 on the DSV3 base, Switch aux 1e-3 on the softmax base); the DSV3 base keeps its expert bias (except the arms marked 'bias removed'). Unlike the aux losses it is measured over the whole global batch and smoothed, and uses probabilities rather than dispatched-token counts, so it does not depend on the micro-batch size. (From arXiv 2605.15403)

Dense layer 0 (the first layer is not MoE)

The MoE of layer 0 is replaced by a plain dense FFN (SwiGLU, width 8 × expert); all other layers unchanged; the dense arms are built on DSV3 SWS.
Zero line = MUONH_FIT: MuonH, fitted LR law (fit), plain CE (no KD), 128-choose-8 MoE, full attention, the vanilla softmax router. Values = line − MUONH_FIT (doc-isolated, paired per seed, q0 = mean of 3 seeds; negative = better).
Negative-entropy balancing φ (phi balancing), coefficient α = 1e-5: every layer keeps an EMA of the router probabilities, me = the long-run mean probability of expert e; loss = α·E·Σe pe·(log me + 1), pe = the mean probability the current tokens give expert e (the bracket carries no gradient). Experts used a lot over time are pushed down and rarely used ones pulled up, driving the routing toward uniform (maximum entropy). Two uses (components in the table below): bias + neg. entropy = DSV3's expert bias (γ = 1e-3) kept, only the seq aux replaced by negative entropy; neg. entropy only = expert bias and seq aux both removed, this term alone. It is measured over the whole global batch, so it does not depend on the micro-batch size (from arXiv 2605.15403; see the 'Negative-entropy balance loss' chapter above).
Verdict: not adopted. The loss is only slightly below DSV3 (the two negative-entropy solid lines sit 0.002–0.006 below the blue solid line), within single-seed noise (about ±0.008); in the full PROD configuration there is almost no difference (PROD1_PHI − PROD1_DPSK: q0 0.000, q1 −0.001, q2 −0.002); with negative entropy only the router is unhealthy (router-health charts below). Runlong made DSV3 the default on 11-03 and stopped all negative-entropy runs.

During training, however, layer 1 (the first MoE layer after the dense one) still has dead experts: about 11–12 in the first half of q2, 18–25 for most of q3, reaching 0 only at the end. DSV3 and bias + negative entropy are healthy with or without the dense layer (dead 0, worst-layer MaxVio ≤ 0.36).
The x axis is the training step; each point summarises all MoE layers at that step (layer mean / worst layer), it is not per layer. The spike of the light-orange solid q4 line (bias + negative entropy · dense layer 0) at step ~44,200 comes from the last two layers (L34 / L35, MaxVio about 8.5, 4 dead experts in L35) and recovers within ~200 steps; at the same step the negative-entropy-only dense run also jumps (from layer 1), the two all-MoE runs do not.

Router choice, SWS architecture, miscellaneous experiments

Zero line = DSV3 SWS (MUONH_FIT_DSV3_SWS): MuonH, fitted LR law (fit), plain CE (no KD), 128-choose-8 MoE, DSV3 router (sigmoid scores + expert bias + seq aux 1e-4, AdamH gate at LR ×1), SWA (5 of 6 layers window 2048) + attention sinks.

Notes

  • Models: the final checkpoints of Boxiang's ladder, re-evaluated by us (document-isolated: every document scored as its own sample).
  • overall_tw pools every split of val_v2, uncheatable, codefresh, v3small, private_internal and pile_test, token-weighted; overall_macro = mean of those six; pile_10k is reported apart. Units: nats/token.
  • CE = cross-entropy only; KD = (1 − α)·CE + α·KL(teacher top-64 + tail ‖ student), teacher MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL. KD's CE reference is the MuonH model of the same recipe (same data order and layout, α = 0).
  • Checked: every suite except private_internal matches Boxiang's doc-isolated results (≤ 0.00005).
  • Full per-model results (incl. 115 splits): trichord/dense_pretrain_result/<Change ID>_<rung>.json.

Best-LR sweeps and fits (MuonH grid, Muon grid, depth × width assumption check). Same data as the doc-isolated tab (our eval).

MuonH learning rate: the best LR in each cell (same MuonH, CE)

This section always uses overall_tsqw (token-sqrt-weighted: all 7 collections - val_v2, uncheatable, codefresh, v3small, private_internal, pile_test, pile_10k - each at its token-weighted loss, averaged with weights ∝ √(scored tokens); weights ≈ uncheatable 31 %, pile_test 23 %, val_v2 15 %, codefresh 13 %, pile_10k 8 %, private_internal 5 %, v3small 5 % - between tw and macro, so neither the longest nor the shortest collection dominates; unlike overall_tw / macro, pile_10k is included); it does not follow the metric toggle above. Each cell = one fixed (model size, training tokens). In a cell, one model per 0.5 / 0.7 / 1 / 1.2 / 1.4 / 2 (/ 2.8 / 4) × the HyperP-law LR; y = loss difference to the cell's 1× (lower is better); the big number = the fitted best multiple m* (the parabola vertex, possibly extrapolated beyond the sampled multiples; m* > 1 means the law is too low), below it the absolute LR η* (in parentheses the cell's 1× LR, i.e. the HyperP-law LR for its depth and training tokens) and how much the optimum beats 1×; the main-ladder TPP 200 cells run along the diagonal; hover a cell to see its LR sweep curve (dashed = parabola in log(multiple), orange = m*). Read a column for depth, the q0 row for training length. Cells have different budgets: compare only within a cell. Blank = not in the design. Every multiple is relative to the ORIGINAL ArchScale law η = 0.016 × (L/8)^−0.5 × (T/10.4B)^−0.32, computed from each run's actual peak LR (not from its Change ID's name), so it does not move if the ladder adopts a new law.

KD loss variants compared: same α 0.8, same MuonH

The 8 runs differ only in how the teacher distribution is truncated in the KD term: α = 0.8, MuonH optimizer, seed 1 and data order are identical; the baseline is still CE (MuonH, α = 0); B64 (top-64 + the rest of the tail as one bucket) is KD α 0.8 itself and is drawn as a line too, so each variant can be read against it. Negative = better than CE.

Naming: letters = tail treatment · number = top-k size · trailing Y = y computed exactly
PartMeaning
BBucket: the tail outside the top-k is merged into one outcome; only the student's total tail mass has to match
SSampled: the tail is estimated from the 4 tokens pre-sampled in the cache (unbiased)
DDData Draw: instead of the teacher's tail, the corpus's actual next token approximates it
DROPTail dropped: the teacher is renormalised over the top-k only (control)
64 / 128how many top-k tokens are computed exactly
Yy exact: when the actual next token y falls outside the top-k, y is taken out of the tail and computed exactly
Δloss (KD variant − CE), lower is better

Zero line = one CE: OPT_MUONH (MuonH old LR, 650B data; q0 = mean of its 3 seeds); all three families are minus this same CE. Each point = the KD arm's seed mean − OPT_MUONH; the 3 q0 seeds are averaged into one point.

Blue vs green: both MiMo-2.6, but LR and KD data both differ (blue uses the 650B data), so their distance is not the LR effect alone. Blue S128Y has q3 only. These are Boxiang-style numbers: the packed validation at the end of training (6 decon sets, mean6 = their plain mean), from the training logs.
